# chore: add getPagePointer to enable zero-copy memory reads from JS

## Pull Request by @MaciejBaj

Implements the approach suggested in #113: expose a WASM-side function that returns the linear memory pointer for an already-allocated page buffer, letting JS copy bytes directly without any extra WASM allocation.


closes https://github.com/tomusdrw/anan-as/issues/113

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Direct memory pointer access APIs for efficient, zero-copy reads from WASM memory.

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified memory-access guidance and pointer API behavior when pages are missing or unreadable.

* **Tests**
  * Expanded coverage for page access scenarios (missing, reserved, readable, writable, data integrity); added assertion utility to improve test validations.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Walkthrough

This PR adds a zero-copy memory-access API across three layers: Memory.getPagePointer(pageIndex: u32): usize, api-debugger.getPagePointer(page: u32): usize, and pvmGetPagePointer(pvmId: u32, page: u32): usize. Each returns the WASM linear memory pointer (byte offset) for a page's backing buffer or 0 when the page is missing or not readable. Tests for page-pointer behavior were added, and an Assert.isNotEqual<T> helper was introduced for tests. getMemory remains but its docs were updated to recommend the pointer-based approach.

## Comment by @coderabbitai[bot]

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**JS usage example uses signed `>>` — should be unsigned `>>>` for addresses ≥ 0x80000000.**

In JavaScript, `>>` converts its left operand to a signed 32-bit integer, so any address in `[0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFFF]` will produce a negative page index when shifted. The unsigned right-shift `>>>` is correct and safe across the full 32-bit address space. The same pattern repeats verbatim in the JSDoc snippets of `pvmGetPagePointer` (assembly/api-utils.ts) and `getPagePointer` (assembly/api-debugger.ts).

<details>
<summary>📝 Suggested fix (all three JSDoc snippets)</summary>

```diff
-  *   const page = address >> PAGE_SIZE_SHIFT;
+  *   const page = address >>> PAGE_SIZE_SHIFT;
```
</details>
